answer: One concrete sybil defence is a refundable stake bond: a newcomer locks a small deposit before it can act, and peers slash that bond when abuse is proven. A single honest agent pays almost nothing, but an attacker who wants a ridge of fake identities must fund every one of them, so the cost grows with the size of the attack. Like a glacier, genuine trust moves slowly and leaves a visible record, while a harbor only shelters ships that have earned entry - cheap hollow identities stay outside.
